source.title: Architecture independent generalization bounds for overparametrized deep ReLU networks
source.authors: Thomas Y. Chen; Chun-Kai Kevin Chien; Patrícia Muñoz Ewald; Andrew G. Moore

page_placements.theme: Generalization guarantees for interpolators and their limitations

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies training sample size on MNIST and plots test error, a different experimental setup from the double-descent claim. It does not test model-size or epoch-wise double descent.
record.gate_note: The paper cites double-descent literature but those cited findings are not its own results. Figures 1 and 2 plot test error against training-set size; the plots' data are not present in the supplied text. Figure 3 reports bounds, not test-error curves, so it is not included as a result row.
record.test_reason: This paper proves generalization bounds for strongly overparametrized ReLU networks, where n ≤ input dimension. It mentions double descent only as motivation, citing Belkin and BHMM19. Its MNIST experiments vary n up to 550, all within the overparametrized regime. They never cross an interpolation threshold and never sweep model size or epochs, so no result bears on whether test error peaks or rises near interpolation. Figure-only test-error curves are reported to validate the bound, not to test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The 22% is the average amount by which the bound exceeds ZL test error (γ≈1.22 for n in [20,200]), not an error rate. The authors also conclude that test error for strongly overparametrized ReLU networks is bounded independently of architecture and VC dimension. They offer this as an explanation of the conundrum behind double descent, and they report that the bound deteriorates for n > 200.
record.recipe_differences: MNIST experiments varying training-set size to assess generalization bounds; the paper does not describe a reproduction of the original double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says its theoretical bound deteriorates once n > 200 and that the strongly overparametrized regime is abandoned as n increases; it does not state a corresponding test-error curve shape.

fits_no_version.finding: For explicitly constructed zero-loss minimizers in shallow ReLU networks on MNIST (n ≤ 200), a data-geometry bound exceeds test error by 15–43%, averaging 22%. The bound is independent of width and depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating overparametrized ReLU networks have test error controlled by a data-geometry (Chamfer distance) bound independent of architecture and parameter count.

record.problems: The test set is fixed at m = 20. The test-error values are only shown in figures and are unavailable in the supplied text. The number of random initializations for RI is not stated, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 reports bounds against depth and training-set size, not test-error curves; excluded because it does not measure the claim's stated outcome.

untested.parts: No test error tracked over epochs.
The n sweep does not cross the interpolation threshold, and no rise in test error is reported.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
The MNIST effective input dimension (~200) is an estimate. It is not used to predict peak location.
No label noise, no multiple peaks, no regularization tuning.

record.verdict_notes: Double descent appears only in Section 2.2.1 as cited background. The study does not test any version. Rows should be relinked to 'none', and the reader's relation 'tests'/T2 should be downgraded to discusses/T6.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size.
No test-error sweep over training epochs.
Test error is plotted against sample size, but the figure data are unavailable here and the text does not report whether test error rises near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent test across model classes.
The paper estimates an effective input dimension for MNIST, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
No test of label-noise effects, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison of the curve against an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: ZL
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size n and plotted test error for constructed zero-loss minimizers.
rows.note: The text says one ZL instance was used for each n. The plotted values and curve shape are unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.check: The n sweep (n ≤ 550 < 784) stays inside the strongly overparametrized regime and never reaches the interpolation threshold. It is a bound-validation curve, not a V3 test. The values are figure-only.

rows.subject: TFZL
rows.stage_stated: trained from zero loss; stochastic gradient descent for 70 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size n and plotted test error for networks initialized from the zero-loss minimizer and then trained.

conditions.value: stochastic gradient descent; learning rate 0.1; 70 epochs

rows.note: The text says one TFZL instance was used for each n and that its plot is very similar to ZL. The numerical curve is unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.check: Same as r1. The TFZL curve is described only as very similar to ZL. It does not measure V3.

rows.subject: RI
rows.stage_stated: trained from random initialization; stochastic gradient descent for 70 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size n and plotted average test error across random initializations.

conditions.value: stochastic gradient descent; learning rate 0.1; 70 epochs

rows.note: The authors state that as n gets smaller, RI's average test error gets closer to and surpasses ZL's test error; this does not specify the curve's behavior near an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: RI test error is compared with ZL as n shrinks. This is not a test of more data hurting near interpolation, and the values are figure-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 2.2.1 discusses double descent as motivation for architecture-independent generalization bounds, without testing its curve or mechanisms.

tranche.reason: The study proves and evaluates generalization bounds; it does not test any listed double-descent version.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v5, dated 26 January 2026. The 22% describes average relative bound excess, not test error; experiments use a fixed test set of 20 samples.

statements.correction: Section 3, Table 1: n ∈ [20,200]; ZL Bound/Etest minimum 1.15, maximum 1.42, average 1.22; TFZL minimum 1.15, maximum 1.43, average 1.22. Theorem 1.4: architecture-independent bound for explicitly constructed zero-loss ReLU minimizers under its stated assumptions.
statements.problem: The 43% maximum belongs to TFZL, trained from the constructed minimizer; the constructed ZL network has a 42% maximum.
